name: reorder-list
title: Reorder list
description: Order again: the products a customer buys regularly, with the last order date, a quantity on every line and a button to add one line or all of them.
docs: Pass items: id, name, an optional variant, image and href, price in minor units (1850 is 18.50) with an optional per ('each', 'per case'), lastOrderedAt (an ISO date), lastQuantity (the quantity starts there, kept inside max) and unavailable, the reason in words for a product that cannot be bought now: its line stays in the list, switched off, with the reason where 'Last ordered' would be. Every line has a checkbox, a quantity and an Add button. onAdd(id, quantity) receives the quantity to add now (return a promise and the button shows it is working; reject and the line says so). The list remembers what it put in the bag, so the number on a line and the number in the bag never disagree: a line that is in the bag says Added with a check, raising its quantity makes the button say 'Add 2 more' and sends only those 2, and lowering it under what is in the bag switches the button off and says 'In bag: 4'. The footer adds up what is still to add in an animated price, and its button calls onAddAll(lines) with every ticked line that has something left to add, each line's quantity being that difference; without onAddAll it calls onAdd for each line. Once everything ticked is in the bag, the footer says what is in the bag. onRemove(id) is called by 'Not interested': the line gives way to 'Removed. Undo' for six seconds and then leaves, and Undo calls onUnremove(id) so you can take the saved choice back. Pass now from the server so 'Last ordered 3 weeks ago' matches in the browser; without it the dates are shown first and the browser's clock turns them into words once the page has loaded. currency, locale and timeZone format the prices and the calendar days. A polite status says what was added and, once ticking settles, what is selected. headingAs and labels do the usual.
